title: Dynamic Routes
summary: Dynamic routes let one folder match many URLs: a **`[param]`** segment captures a single value into `params`, **`[...slug]`** is a catch-all that captures the rest of the path as an array, and **`[[...slug]]`** is an optional catch-all that also matches the parent — and **`generateStaticParams`** pre-renders these pages at build time (SSG).

subtopics.title: [param] — a single dynamic segment
subtopics.explanation: Naming a folder `[id]` turns that URL segment into a parameter. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` matches `/blog/hello` and `/blog/world`, and the captured value arrives in the page's `params` prop as `{ slug: 'hello' }`. One file serves an unbounded set of similar pages — the classic blog/product/user-profile pattern.

subtopics.title: Accessing params in a page
subtopics.explanation: A page (and layout) for a dynamic segment receives a `params` object whose keys are the segment names. In Next 14 you read it synchronously; in newer versions `params` is a Promise you `await`. Use it to fetch the matching record. Layouts and other special files at the same depth get the same `params`.

subtopics.title: [...slug] — catch-all segments
subtopics.explanation: A folder named `[...slug]` matches one OR MORE path segments and collects them into an array. `app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx` matches `/docs/a`, `/docs/a/b`, `/docs/a/b/c` and gives `params.slug = ['a','b','c']`. Great for arbitrarily-deep docs trees or file-path-like URLs. Note: it does NOT match the bare `/docs` parent.

subtopics.title: [[...slug]] — optional catch-all
subtopics.explanation: Doubling the brackets makes the catch-all optional: `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` matches the parent `/shop` (with `params.slug === undefined`) AND `/shop/a/b`. Use it when one page should handle both the index and nested paths — e.g. a category page that also renders the storefront root.

subtopics.title: generateStaticParams — pre-render at build (SSG)
subtopics.explanation: Export an async `generateStaticParams` from a dynamic page to tell Next which param values to pre-render at build time, turning the route into SSG. It returns an array of params objects (e.g. `[{ slug: 'hello' }]`). Combine with ISR (`revalidate`) to refresh them, and control whether unknown params render on-demand or 404 via `dynamicParams`.

subtopics.title: searchParams vs params
subtopics.explanation: `params` are path segments defined by your folder names (`/blog/[slug]`); `searchParams` are the query string (`?page=2&sort=asc`). A page receives both as props. Crucially, reading `searchParams` makes the route dynamic (rendered per request), while `params` alone can stay static via generateStaticParams.

subtopics.title: Typing dynamic params
subtopics.explanation: Type the props so params keys match your folder names: a `[slug]` page uses `{ params: { slug: string } }`, and a catch-all uses `{ params: { slug: string[] } }`. In Next 15+ these become Promises (`Promise<{ slug: string }>`) that you await. Typing catches mismatched param names early.
subtopics.example: type Props = { params: { slug: string[] } }; // for [...slug]

foundations.overview: Dynamic routes let a single file serve many URLs by capturing parts of the path into a `params` object. A `[param]` folder captures one segment; `[...slug]` captures a whole remaining path as an array; `[[...slug]]` does the same but is optional (also matching the parent). For static sites, `generateStaticParams` enumerates the values to pre-render at build time.
foundations.formalDefinition: A dynamic segment is a route folder whose name is wrapped in brackets, mapping the matched path part(s) into the `params` prop: `[name]` → a string, `[...name]` → a non-empty string array, `[[...name]]` → an optional string array. `generateStaticParams` is an exported async function returning the param sets to statically generate.
foundations.whyItMatters: Almost every real app has parameterized URLs — products, posts, users, docs. Dynamic routes are how you build them without one file per page, and knowing single vs catch-all vs optional catch-all, plus when a route is static vs dynamic, is core App Router fluency.
foundations.mentalModel: Think of brackets as 'wildcards in the URL that get handed to you as params.' One `[x]` = one slot; `[...x]` = 'the rest of the path as a list'; `[[...x]]` = 'the rest, or nothing.' generateStaticParams is the build-time list of which wildcard values to bake into static HTML.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser just requests a URL like /blog/hello; Next matches it to the [slug] route and serves either a pre-built static page (if generateStaticParams included it) or renders it on demand. To the browser it's an ordinary page; the dynamic matching happens server-side.
foundations.realWorldUsage: A blog uses `[slug]` with generateStaticParams over all posts (SSG); a docs site uses `[...slug]` for arbitrarily nested pages; a storefront uses `[[...slug]]` so /shop and /shop/category both render from one file; a product page reads `params.id` and `searchParams.variant`.
foundations.businessImpact: Pre-rendering parameterized pages with generateStaticParams gives CDN-fast, SEO-friendly pages for catalogs and content at scale, driving organic traffic — while one maintainable template covers thousands of URLs.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Dynamic segments collapse what would be thousands of files into a single template plus a data fetch, drastically reducing code. Correctly choosing param shapes prevents routing conflicts and 404s.
foundations.performanceImpact: params-only pages can be fully static (generateStaticParams → SSG, optionally ISR), serving from the CDN; reading searchParams opts the route into per-request dynamic rendering, so isolate query-dependent UI to keep the rest static.
commonUseCases: [slug] for blog posts, products, and user profiles
[...slug] for arbitrarily-nested docs or file-path-style URLs
[[...slug]] when one page must serve both the index and nested paths
generateStaticParams to pre-render all known pages as SSG (plus ISR to refresh)

commonMisconceptions.myth: [...slug] also matches the parent route like /docs.
commonMisconceptions.reality: A required catch-all [...slug] matches /docs/a and deeper but NOT the bare /docs. Use the optional catch-all [[...slug]] if you also need to match the parent.

commonMisconceptions.myth: generateStaticParams must list every possible param or the page breaks.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It lists the params to pre-build; by default (dynamicParams = true) other values are rendered on demand at request time. Set dynamicParams = false to 404 anything not listed.

codeLab.title: Implement a catch-all matcher
codeLab.instructions: Complete `matchDocs` so a `[...slug]` route at /docs returns `{ slug: [...] }` for any nested path (but null for the bare /docs). Then Run to see the params for each URL.
hints: A required catch-all needs at least one segment after /docs, so /docs itself should not match.
Split the captured remainder on '/' to build the slug array.

debuggingLab.title: params.slug is undefined / the wrong shape
debuggingLab.symptom: Reading params.slug crashes or is undefined, or .map throws because slug is a string when you expected an array (or vice versa).
debuggingLab.errorAnalysis: Param shape depends on the bracket style: `[slug]` gives a string, but `[...slug]` (and `[[...slug]]`) give a string ARRAY. Calling string methods like toUpperCase on the array throws. You must handle the array — join it for a path, or take the last element — and remember an optional catch-all can be undefined for the parent route.
commonMistakes: Treating a catch-all params.slug (array) as a single string.
Forgetting that an optional catch-all [[...slug]] is undefined on the parent route, then calling array methods on undefined.
debuggingLab.fixChallenge: Handle the array shape: derive the last segment safely and guard against undefined.

theory.question: Explain [param], [...slug], and [[...slug]] dynamic routes and the params each produces.
theory.directAnswer: All three are bracketed route folders. `[slug]` matches a single segment and gives params.slug as a string (e.g. /blog/hello → { slug: 'hello' }). `[...slug]` is a catch-all that matches one or more segments as an array (/docs/a/b → { slug: ['a','b'] }) but NOT the bare parent. `[[...slug]]` is an optional catch-all that matches the same AND the parent route, where params.slug is undefined.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: Three dynamic segment kinds: single ([x] → string), required catch-all ([...x] → string[]), optional catch-all ([[...x]] → string[] | undefined).
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: To serve many URLs from one file: single records, arbitrarily-deep paths, and index-plus-nested from a single page.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: Next matches the URL against the bracketed folder and injects the captured value(s) into the page/layout's params prop.

theory.whyImportant: Choosing the right bracket style avoids 404s and routing conflicts and is a standard intermediate App Router question.
theory.realWorldExample: Blog post = [slug]; nested docs tree = [...slug]; storefront where /shop and /shop/category share a page = [[...slug]].

nestedTopics.title: Parent matching
nestedTopics.explanation: [...slug] excludes the parent; [[...slug]] includes it (slug undefined).

nestedTopics.title: Param shape
nestedTopics.explanation: Single → string; catch-all → string[]; type your props accordingly.

nestedTopics.title: Route precedence
nestedTopics.explanation: More specific static/[param] routes win over catch-alls at the same level.

followUps.question: Which one matches /docs (the parent) as well as nested paths?
followUps.answer: The optional catch-all [[...slug]] — for the parent, params.slug is undefined; for nested paths it's the array of segments.

followUps.question: What type is params.slug for [...slug]?
followUps.answer: A string array (string[]), so handle it with array methods like join or indexing — not string methods.

theory.question: What does generateStaticParams do, and how do dynamicParams and revalidate interact with it?
theory.directAnswer: generateStaticParams is an async function you export from a dynamic page that returns the list of param values to pre-render at build time, turning the route into SSG. By default dynamicParams is true, so a request for a param NOT in the list is rendered on demand at request time (and cached); setting dynamicParams = false makes unlisted params 404. Adding revalidate turns those static pages into ISR, refreshing them on a schedule.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: A build-time enumerator of dynamic params that drives static generation for a dynamic route.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: To get CDN-fast, SEO-friendly static pages for known parameterized URLs (catalogs, posts) without manual per-page files.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: At build, Next calls generateStaticParams, pre-renders one page per returned params object; dynamicParams controls unlisted values, and revalidate adds background regeneration (ISR).

theory.whyImportant: It's the bridge between dynamic routes and static rendering and a frequent discriminator for understanding Next's rendering model.
theory.realWorldExample: A blog returns all post slugs from generateStaticParams with revalidate: 3600, so every post is static and refreshed hourly; new slugs render on demand because dynamicParams stays true.

nestedTopics.title: dynamicParams
nestedTopics.explanation: true (default): render unlisted params on demand; false: 404 them.

nestedTopics.title: ISR pairing
nestedTopics.explanation: Export revalidate to refresh the generated pages without a full rebuild.

nestedTopics.title: Nested params
nestedTopics.explanation: For multiple dynamic segments, return objects with all keys (e.g. { category, slug }).

followUps.question: How do you 404 any param you didn't pre-build?
followUps.answer: Export const dynamicParams = false; then only the params returned by generateStaticParams render, and everything else returns 404.

scenario.question: You have 50,000 product pages that change prices a few times a day and must be fast and SEO-friendly. How do you route and render them?
scenario.directAnswer: Use a `[id]` (or `[slug]`) dynamic route with generateStaticParams to enumerate the products and pre-render them as SSG, plus revalidate (ISR) so prices refresh on a schedule (e.g. hourly) without a full rebuild. Keep dynamicParams = true so newly added products render on demand and get cached. This gives CDN-fast, indexable pages with eventual freshness, and you can add on-demand revalidation when a price actually changes.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: A dynamic route pre-rendered with generateStaticParams and kept fresh with ISR.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: Large catalogs need static speed/SEO but also periodic freshness — pure SSG is too stale, pure SSR too costly.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: Build pre-renders all listed product ids; revalidate triggers background regeneration after the window; dynamicParams allows new ids on demand.

scenario.whyImportant: Combining dynamic routes, SSG, and ISR is the canonical large-catalog solution and a common system-design-flavored question.

nestedTopics.title: On-demand revalidation
nestedTopics.explanation: revalidatePath/Tag refresh specific products the moment data changes.

nestedTopics.title: searchParams caveat
nestedTopics.explanation: If a product page reads searchParams it becomes dynamic; isolate that UI to keep the page static.

followUps.question: What if you can't enumerate all 50k at build time?
followUps.answer: Return a subset (or none) from generateStaticParams and rely on dynamicParams = true so the rest are rendered and cached on first request, optionally with ISR.

coding.question: Write a [slug] blog page that is statically generated with generateStaticParams, 404s unknown slugs, and reads searchParams — with typed params.
coding.thoughtProcess: I'll make app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx. generateStaticParams returns all slugs to pre-build. I'll set dynamicParams = false to 404 unlisted slugs. The page is an async Server Component that awaits the post and calls notFound() if missing. I'll type params as { slug: string } and read searchParams for a small option. (In Next 15+ params/searchParams are Promises to await.)
coding.lineByLine: generateStaticParams returns every slug, so Next pre-renders each post at build (SSG). dynamicParams = false makes unlisted slugs 404; revalidate = 3600 refreshes the static pages hourly (ISR). The page is an async Server Component: it awaits the post and calls notFound() when missing. params is typed { slug: string }; searchParams.comments toggles the comments UI — reading it keeps that branch dynamic while the rest stays static.
coding.timeComplexity: O(n) at build over the post list for generateStaticParams; O(1) data fetch per page.

alternativeApproaches.title: Allow on-demand pages
alternativeApproaches.explanation: Keep dynamicParams = true so unlisted slugs render and cache on first request instead of 404ing.
alternativeApproaches.code: export const dynamicParams = true; // render+cache unknown slugs on demand

followUps.question: How does this change in Next 15+?
followUps.answer: params and searchParams become Promises, so you await them: `const { slug } = await params;` and `const sp = await searchParams;` inside the async component.

productionDeepDive.architecture: Model parameterized URLs with the narrowest bracket that fits: [param] for single records, [...slug] for deep trees, [[...slug]] only when one page must also serve its parent. Pair each dynamic route with generateStaticParams to pre-build known pages and notFound() for missing records, and keep query-dependent UI isolated so reading searchParams doesn't force the whole route dynamic.
productionDeepDive.performance: Prefer SSG via generateStaticParams (plus ISR revalidate) for catalogs and content so pages serve from the CDN; reserve fully dynamic rendering for genuinely per-request pages. Avoid reading searchParams at the page root if most of the page is static — push it into a small client/suspense boundary.
productionDeepDive.security: Treat params and searchParams as untrusted input: validate/parse them before using in queries to prevent injection, and authorize record access on the server. Don't assume a pre-built slug implies authorization; check per request where needed.
productionDeepDive.scaling: generateStaticParams can pre-build huge sets, but enormous catalogs may build a hot subset and rely on dynamicParams = true with ISR for the long tail. On-demand revalidation (revalidatePath/Tag) avoids rebuild storms when individual records change.
productionDeepDive.maintainability: Centralize data access (getPost/getPosts) and type params/searchParams precisely so folder names and code stay in sync. Document each route's bracket choice and rendering mode (SSG/ISR/dynamic) so reviewers understand freshness guarantees.
productionDeepDive.observability: The build output marks each dynamic route static/dynamic and reports how many pages generateStaticParams produced; monitor cache HIT/MISS and ISR regenerations, and track notFound rates to spot bad links or missing pre-builds.

caseStudies.problem: Tens of thousands of parameterized pages needing speed, SEO, and periodic freshness.
caseStudies.solution: [slug] route + generateStaticParams for known pages + ISR revalidate, with dynamicParams handling the long tail.
caseStudies.tradeoffs: Eventual consistency from the revalidate window; build time grows with the pre-built set.
caseStudies.lessons: Match bracket style to the URL shape and lean on generateStaticParams + ISR; reserve dynamic rendering for truly per-request pages.

projectBuilder.summary: Add parameterized routes to the SaaS app: a static blog with [slug], a nested docs tree with [...slug], and a typed product page that reads params and searchParams.
requirements: A [slug] blog route pre-rendered with generateStaticParams (SSG + ISR)
A [...slug] docs route handling arbitrarily nested paths
A product page with typed params and searchParams, 404ing unknown ids
projectBuilder.architecture: Dynamic segments per content type: app/blog/[slug] (SSG via generateStaticParams + revalidate), app/docs/[...slug] (catch-all), app/products/[id] (typed params + notFound). Query-dependent UI is isolated to keep pages mostly static.

app/
  blog/[slug]/page.tsx        // generateStaticParams + revalidate

steps.title: Static blog with [slug]
steps.instructions: Create app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx, add generateStaticParams over all posts, and call notFound() for missing posts.
steps.checkpoint: Build output shows one static page per post; bad slugs 404.

steps.title: Nested docs with [...slug]
steps.instructions: Add app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx and render breadcrumbs from the slug array; confirm /docs/a/b works and /docs alone doesn't match.
steps.checkpoint: Deeply nested doc URLs render with correct breadcrumbs.

steps.title: Typed product page
steps.instructions: Build app/products/[id]/page.tsx with typed params and searchParams (e.g. ?variant=), validating inputs.
steps.checkpoint: params.id is typed/validated and variant from searchParams changes the view.

enhancements: Switch docs to [[...slug]] so /docs renders an index from the same file
Add on-demand revalidation when a post or product changes
interviewQuestions: Why is [...slug] right for docs but [[...slug]] needed if /docs must also render?
How does generateStaticParams plus revalidate make the blog both fast and fresh?

keyTakeaways: [param] captures one segment (params.slug = string); [...slug] is a catch-all capturing the rest as an array; [[...slug]] is an optional catch-all that also matches the parent (slug may be undefined).
params come from the path (folder names); searchParams come from the query string — and reading searchParams makes a route render dynamically.
generateStaticParams returns the param values to pre-render at build time, turning a dynamic route into SSG (pair with revalidate for ISR).
dynamicParams controls unlisted params: true (default) renders them on demand; false returns 404.
Type props to match folder names — { slug: string } for [param] and { slug: string[] } for catch-alls — and remember params/searchParams are Promises to await in Next 15+.
